detail.abstract: We ask when voluntary disclosure about hard-to-verify risks predicts later adverse outcomes. We study this in human-rights due-diligence (HRDD) discussion on UK earnings calls, where direct verication is weak and delayed labor-rights enforcement outcomes provide noisy independent checks on earlier talk. Across UK earnings-call transcripts from 20072024, within-rm increases in HRDD discussion predict next-quarter labor-rights controversies: a one-standard-deviation increase raises next-quarter incident probability by 1.33 pp and expected incident counts by 7.46%. The same discussion also predicts Employment Tribunal cases two years ahead, while workplace-safety prosecutions serve as a placebo with no predictive content. The predictive content is strongest in executive HRDD intensity and in concrete sub-topics (supply chain, remediation); generic stakeholder language and analyst HRDD intensity carry none. Predictive content strengthens after COVID-19 and after the 2020 Boohoo scandal for treated fashion rms, and repeated supply-chain language loses content as it becomes routine. These ndings identify two conditions under which voluntary disclosure about hard-to-verify risks carries information: external scrutiny that makes misrepresentation costly, and language concrete enough to be veriable. The ndings imply that mandating more disclosure without strengthening the institutions that verify it may produce more talk without more information.

title: Temporal Scaling with Stacked Ensembles for Cost-Per-Purchase Advertising Forecasts
affiliations: Auburn University, Auburn University, National Central University, Auburn University at Montgomery and Auburn University

detail.title: Temporal Scaling with Stacked Ensembles for Cost-Per-Purchase Advertising Forecasts
detail.abstract: We study temporal scaling for purchase and cost prediction in Cost-Per-Purchase (CPP) digital advertising, where campaign durations vary substantially and complicate forecasting. Using a proprietary dataset of 30,380 campaigns, we evaluate a temporal-scaling workflow with tree-based learners and a stacked ensemble under both same-scale and fixed-horizon forecasting settings. The approach improves forecasting accuracy, with the largest gains appearing in 30-day planning scenarios and in high-value campaigns that account for most revenue and spend. Experiments on four public datasets further validate the method’s scope: it improves prediction of duration-scalable targets--continuous cumulative outcomes whose magnitude grows with exposure duration and correctly defaults to the baseline for binary or per-event targets that lack this structure. Temporal scaling is best deployed as a conditionally applied preprocessing step for variable-duration cumulative regression, with the accompanying log-correlation diagnostic identifying when the transformation is appropriate.

title: From Fear to Fury: The Behavioral Trade-offs of Removing Negative Feedback Option in Online Discussion Platforms
affiliations: McGill University - Desautels Faculty of Management, , McGill University - Desautels Faculty of Management and HEC Montréal

detail.title: From Fear to Fury: The Behavioral Trade-offs of Removing Negative Feedback Option in Online Discussion Platforms
detail.abstract: Peer evaluation systems are central to online platforms, enabling users to assess and respond to content. While negative feedback tools, such as downvotes, aim to improve content quality, they may also suppress expression or foster toxicity. This study investigates the behavioral effects of removing the downvote option using a natural experiment from a large North American discussion forum. Leveraging a difference-indifferences-in-time design and matrix completion estimator, we find that downvote removal decreased user participation, while increasing average post length, indicating greater effort among remaining users. At the same time, emotional expression rose and toxicity increased, especially through profanity and insults. Heterogeneity analyses reveal that low-engagement users drove toxicity increases, while high-engagement users disproportionately disengaged. At the topic level, downvote removal reduced cross-user discussion diversity but improved within-post focus and alignment with ongoing conversations. A complementary user survey corroborates these findings and points to two psychological mechanisms: reduced fear of negative evaluation and heightened psychological reactance. Overall, these results highlight the nuanced trade-offs in content moderation design and offer actionable insights for platform governance.

title: Following the Scent: How Attention-grabbing Verbal Cues in Headlines Shape Fake News Believability
affiliations: , McGill University and McGill University - Desautels Faculty of Management

detail.title: Following the Scent: How Attention-grabbing Verbal Cues in Headlines Shape Fake News Believability
detail.abstract: The increasing spread of fake news on social media raises important questions about the factors that lead individuals to believe misinformation. Although prior research has emphasized the influence of several user-level characteristics and presentation formats, the impact of attention-grabbing verbal cues, a commonly used feature in practice, remains underexplored. Drawing on information foraging theory and the influence of presumed influence model, we conceptualize attention-grabbing verbal cues (e.g., an "Exclusive tag") as information scents that shape users' cognitive evaluations of fake news. Across three complementary studies, we examine how such cues affect believability judgments. The first study uses real-world fake news data to show that articles with headlines containing attention-grabbing verbal cues are consumed more. We then conduct two controlled experiments to demonstrate that the presence of those labels increases believability by enhancing individuals' presumed beliefs about others and further examine the moderating role of different types of engagement metrics. Overall, our findings illustrate how informational and social signals jointly influence belief formation in digital ecosystems, advancing theory on fake news consumption and offering practical implications for responsible headline design and platform governance.

title: The Correction Trilemma: A Diagnostic Heuristic for Trade-offs in Epistemic Systems
affiliations: RO Educational Institute

detail.title: The Correction Trilemma: A Diagnostic Heuristic for Trade-offs in Epistemic Systems

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No commercial, institutional, or financial conflicts of interest are declared.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This theoretical and diagnostic research involved no human participants, animal subjects, or collection of personally identifiable information. Experimental components consisted exclusively of controlled interactions with publicly accessible AI systems in accordance with their terms of service. Ethics committee approval was not required under standard guidelines. All analyses are based on published literature, publicly available AI outputs, and established philosophical frameworks.
declarations.funderStatement: No financial support was received. The work was conducted independently and self-funded.

detail.abstract: Epistemic systems-distributed configurations of human agents, algorithms, data infrastructures, and institutions that collectively generate, filter, and revise knowledge claimsexhibit persistent tensions among three capacities: registration (the entry of counterevidence into the formal record), traceability (the ability to locate errors to their specific sources), and receptivity (the capacity to sustain heterodox claims and implement corrective actions). This paper introduces the Correction Trilemma as a diagnostic heuristic for identifying such tensions and guiding institutional reflection. Under realistic constraints-bounded rationality, finite resources, and functional interdependence-efforts to strengthen any two of these capacities often impose costs on the third. The term "trilemma" is used to denote this recurring pattern of trade-offs, not an impossibility theorem. The framework provides a conceptual vocabulary and three pathological patterns (Corrective Chaos, Elite Dogmatism, Analytical Paralysis) that help diagnose which dimension is systematically sacrificed. We illustrate the heuristic through case studies drawn from psychology's replication crisis, AI-based medical diagnosis, and climate modeling intercomparisons (CMIP), showing how trade-offs can be managed but not eliminated. The framework is offered as a complement to existing philosophical and metascience work-a common language for analyzing correction dynamics, anticipating unintended consequences of reforms, and designing more self-aware epistemic systems.

title: How Platform Design Drives Repurchase in B2C E-Commerce:The Selective Mediating Role of Trust

detail.title: How Platform Design Drives Repurchase in B2C E-Commerce:The Selective Mediating Role of Trust
detail.abstract: Purpose – The prevailing assumption in e-commerce trust research is that consumer trust mediates the effects of platform design features on repurchase intentions in a broadly uniform way. This study tests that assumption directly, arguing and demonstrating that trust mediates selectively — strongly for credibility-signalling platform features and not at all for transactional-incentive features. Seven structural platform variables are examined: online product recommendations (OPR), structural assurance (SA), free shipping (FS), vendor-specific guarantees (VSG), return policy (RP), payment on delivery (POD), and website quality (WQ).Design/Methodology/Approach – Primary survey data were collected from 419 active B2C e-commerce consumers in India. Structural equation modelling (SEM) was conducted in AMOS 24 using bootstrapped mediation testing (2,000 samples) to obtain direct, indirect, and total effect estimates for each system variable pathway through trust to repurchase intentions. The 48-item instrument was validated through expert panel review and pilot-study item purification, with Cronbach’s alpha values exceeding .80 across all constructs.Findings – Trust mediates the platform feature–repurchase relationship selectively rather than universally. Return policy (indirect β = .249), structural assurance (β = .153), and website quality (β = .129) exert significant mediated effects through trust. Vendor-specific guarantees (β = .354) and payment on delivery (β = −.152) drive repurchase directly and independently of trust. Trust is the most powerful direct predictor of repurchase intentions (β = .687, p < .001).Practical Implications – Platform managers should treat return policy, structural assurance, and website quality as trust-building investments that generate repurchase by first establishing consumer confidence in the vendor. Vendor-specific guarantees and payment on delivery operate as direct purchase incentives that bypass trust formation and require a distinct management logic. As digital payment adoption deepens in India, the strategic weight of trust-based retention features will increase.Originality/Value – This study makes three contributions. First, it provides the first AMOS-based bootstrapped mediation evidence challenging the universalist trust-mediation assumption across seven platform-level predictors in an integrated model. Second, it establishes a theoretically coherent typology distinguishing trust-pathway from direct-incentive platform features. Third, it contributes primary evidence from the Indian B2C e-commerce context — the world’s most consequential digitally transitioning consumer market — that enriches and qualifies generalisations derived from Western and East Asian samples.

title: The Impact of Re-election After Demotion on Block Validations in Committee-based Consensus Blockchain Platform
affiliations: , McGill University - Desautels Faculty of Management and McGill University - Desautels Faculty of Management

detail.title: The Impact of Re-election After Demotion on Block Validations in Committee-based Consensus Blockchain Platform
detail.abstract: Committee-based consensus (CBC) protocols, in which blockchain validation is delegated to a selected group of participants, are increasingly employed in blockchain platforms to enhance efficiency. Prominent CBC protocols use a voting system that allows users to elect (or demote) committee members responsible for block validation. Previous literature has focused on the voting process, particularly on how committee members are elected by blockchain participants through voting mechanisms. We extend this literature by exploring the implications of voting mechanisms that allow existing committee members to be demoted and subsequently re-elected. Specifically, we examine whether and how their block validation performance is affected after being demoted and re-elected, as measured by the number of missed blocks during transaction verification. Using a quasi-experimental research design, we show that the number of missed blocks in transaction verification significantly decreases after a committee member is re-elected following a demotion. Interestingly, this effect appears to be driven by an increase in vote withdrawals from prior supporters. As the number of vote withdrawals from previous supporters rises, re-elected committee members tend to miss fewer blocks in transaction verifications. These findings have important implications for the viability of voting systems in CBC protocols that permit both election and demotion of committee members. They also provide valuable insights for blockchain developers in designing more effective voting systems for CBC protocols.

title: Media Pressure and Abnormal Returns in Cryptocurrency Markets Evidence from Global News Data (GDELT) and the Bitcoin Media Pressure Index (BMPI)

detail.title: Media Pressure and Abnormal Returns in Cryptocurrency Markets Evidence from Global News Data (GDELT) and the Bitcoin Media Pressure Index (BMPI)
detail.abstract: This paper introduces a novel index (BMPI) designed to quantify media-driven price distortions in cryptocurrency markets. Using 3,800 daily observations from 7 September 2015 to 31 January 2026, it constructs the Bitcoin Media Pressure Index (BMPI) from GDELT Global Knowledge Graph (GKG) 2.0 metadata and links it to a returns-based abnormal-return decomposition. Across 29 identified Bitcoin price peaks, the mean media contribution within event windows is 16.86% of abnormal returns, while the associated effect half-life reaches 32.9 days. Granger predictability tests show that media volume significantly precedes anomalous price effects, with balanced-preset F-statistics of 17.78 at lag 1, 34.45 at lag 3, 20.67 at lag 5, and 13.91 at lag 7 (all p < 0.001). Out-of-sample validation on 2022-2025 data yields r = 0.636 with R2 degradation of only -18.1%, and a rolling walk-forward design across 114 windows produces mean out-of-sample correlation of r = 0.714. Benchmark comparison with the Crypto Fear and Greed Index (CFGI) shows low overlap (r = 0.164) and an incremental R2 gain of +0.039, indicating that BMPI captures a media-specific informational dimension distinct from composite sentiment. The evidence is consistent with the view that media pressure operates as a short-run amplification channel in cryptocurrency price formation rather than as a long-run equilibrium force. All code and data are publicly available for reproducibility.

title: Design-based Refinement of an LLM-powered Conversational Learning Simulation for Customer Validation in Entrepreneurship Education
affiliations: Ateneo de Manila University, Ateneo de Manila University, Ateneo de Manila University, Ateneo de Manila University and Ateneo de Manila University

detail.title: Design-based Refinement of an LLM-powered Conversational Learning Simulation for Customer Validation in Entrepreneurship Education

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no competing interests. This paper is derived from the first author's doctoral dissertation completed at Ateneo de Manila University.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study was approved by the Ateneo de Manila University Institutional Review Board (also known as the University Research Integrity Office). Informed consent was obtained from all participants.

detail.abstract: Traditional entrepreneurship education methods struggle to capture the nonlinear, experiential nature of customer validation-the process of determining whether a product genuinely addresses a market need. This paper presents the design, iterative refinement, and evaluation of VentureBot, an LLM-powered conversational learning simulation supporting customer validation practice for technology entrepreneurship students. Employing design-based research across two classroom deployments, we show how diagnostic null findings from Phase 1 (n = 109 matched pairs) motivated targeted refinements yielding significant results in Phase 2 (n = 46 matched pairs). Phase 2 detected statistically significant pre-to-post increases in four application-oriented competencies: Target Market Understanding (p = 0.002), Market Research (p = 0.024), Business Model Iteration (p = 0.001), and Lean Canvas Application (p = 0.002). Qualitative findings revealed shifts from confirmation-oriented to interrogationoriented conceptions of validation, with 84% of students endorsing iterative feedback as the most valued design feature. We propose the Grounding-Alignment-Behavior Framework to explain concentrated learning gains, derive design implications for conversational learning simulations, and argue that such systems are most effective as complements to human mentorship rather than standalone replacements.

title: Examining the Efficacy of Peer Punishment in Online Content Moderation
affiliations: University at Buffalo (SUNY) - School of Management, McGill University - Desautels Faculty of Management and McGill University - Desautels Faculty of Management

detail.title: Examining the Efficacy of Peer Punishment in Online Content Moderation
detail.abstract: Social platforms moderate content in many ways, including temporarily suspending user accounts. We study a peer-driven variant, "peer bans," in which platform users collectively trigger the suspension of their peers, and examine how it shapes subsequent participation and content characteristics. Using proprietary data from a large discussion platform, we find sizable declines in posting after a peer ban, while posts after the ban are more negative in sentiment. Effects are weaker among long-tenured users and those with less positive feedback history. We interpret these patterns through inequity theory, which links motivation to perceived fairness in settings where evaluations are driven by perceptions rather than anchored in objective metrics. To examine why these changes occur, we conduct three tests. First, a near-ban placebo shows that substantial peer negative evaluation without an actual suspension does not reproduce post-suspension patterns. Second, analyses of suspended users’ outward actions toward others show declines in both negative and positive evaluations, with no significant change in targeted negative evaluations, consistent with withdrawal rather than retaliation. Third, a scenario-based experiment varying perceived post type and suspension parameters shows that lower perceived fairness and proportionality are associated with lower motivation to re-engage. Overall, the evidence supports an explanation based on inequity theory. We discuss design implications for platform administrators, highlighting trade-offs between scalable peer enforcement and downstream engagement.

title: Risks of AI-Driven Vulnerability Identification, Exploitation, and Code Exposure
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Risks of AI-Driven Vulnerability Identification, Exploitation, and Code Exposure
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence is fundamentally reshaping the cybersecurity threat landscape, creating a paradox in which the same technologies that strengthen defensive operations simultaneously empower adversaries with unprecedented offensive capabilities. This paper provides a comprehensive examination of AI's dual-use impact on vulnerability identification and exploitation, with particular attention to the emerging risks associated with code repositories, AI-assisted software development, and secrets sprawl across enterprise environments. Drawing on threat intelligence from IBM X-Force, Cisco Talos, GitGuardian, and academic research through early 2026, this paper documents how AI is compressing the vulnerability exploitation lifecycle, democratizing cyber offense, and introducing novel attack surfaces through AIgenerated code and compromised development infrastructure. The findings reveal that nearly 29 million hardcoded secrets were exposed on public GitHub repositories in 2025 alone, a 34% year-over-year increase, while AI-assisted code commits leak credentials at roughly double the baseline rate. The paper proposes a comprehensive risk mitigation framework organized around ten pillars and discusses the regulatory landscape, including the EU AI Act (enforceable August 2026), the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, and ISO/IEC 42001. The paper concludes with actionable recommendations for organizations seeking to defend against AI-augmented threats while responsibly leveraging AI for security operations.

title: When AI Writes the Reviews: Generative AI and the Changing Nature of User-Generated Content in Online Markets

detail.title: When AI Writes the Reviews: Generative AI and the Changing Nature of User-Generated Content in Online Markets

detail.abstract: The launch of ChatGPT in November 2022 reduced the cost of producing written content to near zero, with consequences for online review ecosystems that remain poorly understood. Using an interrupted time series design on nearly 50 million Amazon reviews across ten categories, we find that reviews became longer, progressively less helpful, and more similar to one another within category-month bins. An endogenous structural break test places the helpfulness break date exactly on December 2022 without imposing it, and a sentence-BERT measure of between-review similarity reverses a pre-existing diversification trend at the same date, providing a length-independent homogenization result. We develop a theory of AI-substitutability predicting that these effects concentrate where review content can be produced without genuine product experience. Consistent with this prediction, the effects on length and similarity are larger for search goods than for experience goods, reversing the demand-side expectation. An enumeration of all 252 possible category partitions and a continuous LLM-derived substitutability score validate the construct for the linguistic outcomes but not for helpfulness, and a reviewer-panel decomposition on 2 million cross-period contributors explains why: AI content enters the corpus via new contributors, while the resulting helpfulness dilution propagates across the corpus and affects even established reviewers. AI-substitutability gates entry, not downstream dilution. The findings are consistent with generative AI eroding the informational foundations of online markets where review content is most substitutable by machine-generated text, with implications for platform design, consumer behavior, and regulatory policy.

title: From Digital Cooperation to Shared Digital Futures: Asia's Role in Rewiring Global Governance for the Age of AI and Quantum

detail.title: From Digital Cooperation to Shared Digital Futures: Asia's Role in Rewiring Global Governance for the Age of AI and Quantum

detail.abstract: Global digital cooperation is entering an implementation phase shaped by the WSIS+20 outcome, the Global Digital Compact, UNESCO's Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence, and the growing institutionalization of digital governance across regions. Yet the governance challenge is no longer merely to "connect the unconnected"; it is to align digital inclusion, trustworthy AI, secure infrastructures, and scientific capacity with sustainable development under conditions of geopolitical fragmentation, widening capability gaps, and accelerating technological change. This paper argues that Asia is not just a beneficiary of global digital cooperation, but a crucible in which the next architecture of cooperation will be tested. Drawing on recent WSIS and UN documents, regional digital policy developments, and the emerging science-forsustainability agenda, it advances a three-part thesis: first, effective digital cooperation must be implementation-oriented, not declaratory; second, Asia's experience with digital scale, diversity, and governance experimentation provides globally relevant design lessons; and third, initiatives such as Quantum Nexus Initiative (QNI) and the GXS Sustainable AI Portal can operationalize ethical quantum-AI governance, open science, and capacity-building for the Global South. The paper concludes with policy recommendations for multilevel actors and identifies pathways to embed science, ethics, and inclusion into WSIS Action Lines and beyond.

title: Persistent Memory Architectures for Personal Artificial Intelligence Systems

detail.title: Persistent Memory Architectures for Personal Artificial Intelligence Systems
detail.abstract: Recent advances in large language models have significantly expanded the capabilities of conversational artificial intelligence systems. Transformer-based architectures enable models capable of reasoning, summarization, and natural language interaction across a wide range of domains. Despite these advances, most deployed systems remain fundamentally stateless. Interactions are typically constrained by bounded context windows and lack persistent understanding of individual users. This limitation restricts the development of truly personal artificial intelligence systems capable of long-term interaction, adaptation, and cognitive support. Human cognition develops across time through accumulated experiences and reflection. Artificial intelligence systems that cannot store and interpret long-term memory remain limited in their ability to support these processes. This paper proposes a conceptual framework for persistent memory in personal artificial intelligence systems. We introduce a layered memory architecture consisting of conversational memory, semantic memory, and reflective memory. These memory layers enable artificial intelligence systems to maintain evolving representations of individuals and support long-term interaction. Persistent memory architectures may therefore represent a foundational component of next-generation personal artificial intelligence systems designed to augment human reflection, decision-making, and cognitive processes.

title: Cross-Model Consistency in Cognitive Structure Measurement: Evidence for Structural Invariance in the RHIS Five-Dimensional Framework Across Different Large Language Models

detail.title: Cross-Model Consistency in Cognitive Structure Measurement: Evidence for Structural Invariance in the RHIS Five-Dimensional Framework Across Different Large Language Models

detail.abstract: This paper reports an empirical observation concerning the cross-model consistency of cognitive structure measurements produced by the RHIS (Refine Humanistic Intelligence System) fivedimensional framework. The RHIS framework measures human cognitive structure across five dimensions: Logic (L), Judgement (J), Emotion (E), Action (A), and Expression (X). These dimensions are defined not as absolute capability scores but as proportional tendency distributions-the relative weight each dimension carries in an individual's cognitive operation. Using identical input data derived from two behavioral questionnaires and a structured conversational record from a single research subject, two independent large language model systems-Claude (Anthropic) and ChatGPT (OpenAI)-were prompted to produce RHIS fivedimensional cognitive profiles independently and without knowledge of each other's outputs. The resulting profiles showed near-identical dimensional values, with an absolute mean difference of 0.12 across all five dimensions and zero difference on the Expression dimension. Critically, the rank ordering of all five dimensions was identical across both systems, and both independently identified Emotion (E) as the dominant axis. We argue that this cross-model consistency constitutes evidence that the RHIS five-dimensional framework captures structural facts about human cognition rather than artifacts of any particular language model's training distribution. The paper discusses the theoretical implications of this finding for AI-assisted cognitive profiling, the methodological significance of dimensional rankorder invariance as a validity criterion, and the distinction between the semantic extraction layer (performed by LLMs) and the structural computation layer (performed by the RHIS independent calculation engine). This is the first formally documented case in a planned series of cross-model consistency observations. Limitations of the single-subject design and directions for future investigation are discussed.

detail.abstract: Residency programs must design resident shift schedules that meet strict regulatory requirements while managing uncertainty in demand and resident availability. Manual scheduling and existing models that ignore uncertainty frequently lead to understaffing and compliance violations. Motivated by a collaboration with a residency program, we study the resident shift scheduling problem (RSSP) and introduce a stochastic optimization framework that integrates backup coverage decisions with regular and on-call assignments while accounting for uncertainty in demand and resident absenteeism. We formulate the RSSP as a two-stage stochastic mixed-integer program. In the first stage, residents are assigned to regular, on-call, and backup duties while satisfying operational, educational, and regulatory constraints. In the second stage, uncertainty in demand and resident availability is realized, and the planned schedule is evaluated to measure understaffing. The objective is to minimize the sum of assignment-related penalties and the expected understaffing. To solve the model, we develop an enhanced logic-based integer decomposition algorithm and derive valid inequalities that significantly tighten the formulation. We implement the proposed framework in a user-friendly decision-support tool designed for practical use by residency programs. Extensive computational experiments on a diverse set of realistic instances demonstrate the scalability and effectiveness of our framework, as well as the value of integrated primary-backup scheduling in improving shift scheduling. Importantly, results show that incorporating structured backup coverage can reduce the risk of understaffing by up to 98% while maintaining full compliance with regulatory requirements. In contrast, common scheduling practices and existing models result in substantial understaffing and compliance violations.

detail.abstract: We study investment in a stock market with unobservable regimes that represent different market states. Our approach first estimates a model for the market and then applies model predictive control to derive the optimal investment policy. As the data are highly noisy, the popular Expectation–Maximization (EM) algorithm can perform poorly in recovering the underlying dynamics. To address this challenge, we extend the value-aware learning framework of Li et al. (2025), originally developed for fully observable systems, to a partially observable setting. Our method learns a model whose value function matches the empirical rewards collected from the real environment as closely as possible. To implement this idea efficiently, we minimize a surrogate loss constructed using the backward stochastic differential equation formulation of the value process together with the variational approximation technique from machine learning. We prove that the resulting estimator converges to the true model. Empirically, we show that our method estimates market parameters substantially more accurately and delivers a superior investment policy under the mean–variance criterion compared with widely used alternatives, including the EM algorithm.

detail.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence into defence institutions is proceeding without a principled framework for distinguishing which cognitive functions admit AI augmentation, which require human oversight, and which must remain exclusively human. This paper proposes a formal ontology that decomposes defence operations into four classes of cognitive primitives-each defined by distinct truth conditions, error tolerances, and computational reducibility-and applies this framework to the specific operational, security, and sovereignty requirements of Indian defence institutions. We demonstrate that AI integration succeeds or fails based on primitive classification accuracy, not technological capability. A logistics calculation mishandled by a probabilistic model is not an efficiency failure-it is a potential operational catastrophe. A command decision outsourced to an algorithm is not automation-it is an abdication of legal and moral authority. By mapping the complete cognitive stack of defence operations-from deterministic computation to irreducibly human command judgment-we establish a framework for building AI-augmented defence institutions that amplify rather than replace human intelligence, while maintaining complete data sovereignty on Indian-controlled infrastructure. This ontology serves as the theoretical and operational foundation for India's Atmanirbhar AI capability in defence-not as a policy aspiration, but as a deployable architecture.

detail.abstract: We develop a model of price competition with procrastinating consumers in which market discipline is supposed to arise from both the initial selection of providers and the possibility of switching providers. As in other theories, consumers may forego large gains by sticking with their initially chosen offer, so competition at the switching stage is weak. Unlike in other theories, consumers - who falsely expect to switch soon - may also fail to select the best starting offer, so competition at the initial stage is weak as well. This mechanism can translate temporary product differentiation into permanently high prices, greatly enhance the price effect of persistent differentiation, or generate high markups even with perfect substitutes. Reflecting the same mechanism, sign-up deals do not serve their classically hypothesized role of returning ex-post profits to consumers, but instead often exacerbate the failure of price competition. We complement our analysis with a tailored survey of consumers, confirming the logic of procrastination underlying our model. Consumer procrastination thus emerges as a novel source of competition failure that applies where other theories do not, helping to explain high average prices in many markets with switching costs.

detail.abstract: Established methods for costing social and behavioural interventions — including the Ingredients Method (Levin, 1975; Levin et al., 2018), cost-feasibility analysis, and prospective cost analysis — specify that resource and cost appraisal should be conducted before programme design is committed, not retrospectively. Yet standard applications of the Behaviour Change Wheel (BCW) place cost considerations at the APEASE stage, after behavioural diagnosis and intervention selection. In commissioned programme design — where budget and target population are defined before design begins — this sequencing creates a structural gap: diagnostic work is undertaken before financial feasibility is known, generating options that may be behaviourally appropriate but structurally unaffordable. This article argues that cost-feasibility analysis, expressed as Cost per Target Person (CTP), should function as the first filter in BCW-based design for this class of situation rather than as a downstream check. CTP is not a new metric; it is the prospective design-stage application of cost per participant — the standard output of the Ingredients Method — benchmarked against published unit-cost estimates. The article further argues that macro-economic frameworks — QALY thresholds and ICER analysis — are legitimate upper-order justification structures but remain operationally remote from design-stage decisions unless translated into a practical ceiling. The Design Feasibility Ratio (DFR), derived from NICE threshold logic, provides that translation. The article also distinguishes burden-side justification from design-stage admissibility: DALY-type burden metrics establish the scale of loss associated with the target problem, whereas CTP and DFR establish whether a proposed design is financially and economically plausible before commitment. Beyond cost sequencing, the article argues that a viable design framework must address two further questions that standard BCW practice leaves implicit: first, at what level should correction occur — in the subject, the intervention, the system, or the economic-operability layer; and second, whether the intended mechanism can transfer from the intervention context into the target-use environment. A correction-locus layer and a Shepard-type transfer analogue are introduced to address these questions. The article’s contribution is positional and conditional, not universal: it argues that established tools, resequenced and extended, convert behavioural architecture into an operational investment framework for the important class of commissioned programmes in which budget constraints are known before design begins.

detail.abstract: Switch machines are critical equipment in railway signaling systems, and their operating condition is closely related to train safety. However, early-stage mechanical degradation is difficult to detect using conventional monitoring methods. To address this issue, a health indicator (HI) construction method based on single-channel acoustic signals is proposed to characterize degradation during the unlocking-to-locking process. The raw signal is first decomposed using sequential variational mode decomposition (SVMD), and effective components are selected based on correlation and kurtosis criteria. Fast independent component analysis (FastICA) combined with symmetrized dot pattern (SDP) is then used to extract representative signal components. Subsequently, multi-domain acoustic features with physical interpretability are constructed, and a cumulative transformation is applied to enhance degradation trends. A dynamic time warping (DTW)-based local linear embedding (LLE) method is further employed for feature fusion to generate the HI. The performance of the HI is evaluated using monotonicity, robustness, and correlation metrics. Based on the constructed HI, particle filtering is applied for remaining useful life (RUL) prediction, and a Bayesian network is developed to support maintenance decision-making. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively characterize degradation and provides a feasible solution for condition monitoring and predictive maintenance of switch machines.

detail.abstract: In early 2026, the author used Gemini Advanced to plan family visits to Reykjavik and Seville. Finding a McDonald's in an unfamiliar city has never been difficult; the chains have the visibility infrastructure. Finding the right independent restaurant in a city you have never visited, matched to your occasion, your family's dietary preferences, and your precise location-that problem has just changed category. It is no longer a search problem. It is an inference problem. And the infrastructure that serves inference at commercial scale does not yet exist. detail.abstract: As large language models are increasingly used in evaluative settings for their conversational potential in interviews, systematic frameworks for assessing their methodological quality are still lacking. Drawing on evaluation, qualitative interviewing, and validity theories, this study develops a theory-grounded framework for evaluating the quality of AI-mediated interviewing in evaluation contexts. This framework is then operationalized into eight assessment measures and applied in a convergent mixed-methods design to compare six generative AI models (five prompted-only and one fine-tuned) across two realistic evaluation interview scenarios. Findings reveal that AI models reliably detected and probed incomplete or irrelevant responses, and the fine-tuned model matched human performance on nearly 70% of quality measures. detail.title: Risk Intelligence - A New Era for Capital Markets
detail.abstract:
This paper proposes a unified risk intelligence framework that combines Mandelbrot's Multifractal Model of Asset Returns (MMAR, 1997) with large language model (LLM) agentic orchestration to address three persistent failures in institutional risk management: Gaussian distributional assumptions that systematically understate tail risk, static VaR scaling rules that misestimate multi-day risk horizons, and the concentration of advanced quantitative risk capabilities within a small number of heavily resourced institutions.

The framework operates across three risk dimensions — market risk, counterparty credit risk (CCR), and liquidity risk — with original contributions in each. For market risk, the Hurst exponent H and tail index α are used to dynamically size Taleb's barbell strategy, replacing heuristic allocation with fractal parameter-driven positioning. For CCR, fractal Potential Future Exposure (PFE) is shown to exceed Gaussian PFE by 25–50% at long horizons, revealing systematic mispricing in dealer XVA charges; a Clayton copula model detects wrong-way risk clustering before it appears in market prices. For liquidity risk, Liquidity-at-Risk (LaR) is rescaled by T^H rather than √T, correcting a persistent underestimation in Basel LCR stress scenarios, while Hurst-regime-dependent execution strategies optimize market impact across asset classes.

An LLM agent layer — operating above the deterministic fractal computation engine via Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool calling — synthesizes unstructured signals (news, earnings, on-chain data, counterparty filings) to detect regime shifts before they appear in price data. The separation between the deterministic engine (source of truth for all quantitative outputs) and the LLM layer (narrative intelligence and tool orchestration) eliminates hallucination risk in the computational path.

The paper proposes a three-tier federated platform architecture (Cloud SaaS, Federated PaaS, Enterprise License) to democratize access to fractal risk intelligence beyond the small number of institutions that currently possess it. A partnership thesis with frontier AI firms (Anthropic, Google DeepMind) is advanced on the basis that fractal risk provides uniquely valuable LLM training signal: every intermediate calculation has a provably correct answer, generating verifiable ground truth for multi-step quantitative reasoning, agentic tool orchestration, long-context regulatory reasoning, and calibrated uncertainty expression — capabilities that transfer across all domains.

The mathematical foundation draws on Mandelbrot (1997) and Taleb (2012). The system architecture, LLM integration layer, fractal barbell sizing rules, asset-class value map, fractal CCR and liquidity risk frameworks, and platform design are original work by the author. No backtesting results are presented; empirical validation across historical stress regimes is identified as the primary next step.

detail.abstract: This study empirically examines how firms’ environmental and social (E and S) activities affect labor productivity using E and S metrics provided by the Korea Corporate Governance Service (KCGS). Using a panel of listed firms over 2015–2023, we find that both the ES rating and the ES score are significantly and negatively associated with labor productivity, which remains robust when we use the overall ESG rating or the E and S pillar ratings. We further provide channel evidence consistent with a cost-burden mechanism: firms with higher ES exhibit a higher total operating cost ratio (TOCR), suggesting that the ES–productivity relationship may be linked to operating cost pressure. Subcategory analyses reveal heterogeneous pathways within ES. In the environmental category, operational/management and communication-oriented activities are negatively related to labor productivity, consistent with higher coordination and management costs. In contrast, community engagement in the social category is positively related to labor productivity, pointing to a complementary pathway through trust, reputation, and relationship capital. Finally, firm- and industry-level analyses indicate substantial heterogeneity in the ES–productivity relationship across firms and industries. Overall, by combining cost-based channel evidence, subcategory-level decompositions, and heterogeneity analyses, this study highlights that evaluating the economic implications of sustainability initiatives requires attention not only to aggregate ES/ESG metrics but also to cost structure, activity types, and firm and industry characteristics.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the role of institutional factors in shaping taxpayer behaviour, using survey data from approximately 70,000 individuals across 29 Sub-Saharan African countries in 2011 and 2016. The results show that individuals are more likely to comply with tax obligations when they perceive greater difficulties in evading taxes, have confidence in the tax administration, and view it as less corrupt. Compliance is also higher when respondents perceive higher-quality public goods and services and do not perceive ethnic discrimination in government policies. We present heterogeneous analysis based on the natural resource abundance status of respondents' countries.

detail.title: Resilience Enhancement and Black Start Strategy for Plateau Comprehensive Energy Systems Based on Multi-timescale Situation Awareness
detail.abstract: High-altitude plateau comprehensive energy systems (P-CES) face severe inherent challenges, including persistently low air density, extreme temperature fluctuations, complex terrain, and inherently weak grid structures. These harsh conditions permanently degrade the thermodynamic performance of energy infrastructure, aggravate renewable energy volatility, intensify peak-shaving difficulties, and sharply heighten the risk of large-scale cascading blackouts. To address these operational pain points, this paper proposes an efficient optimization framework integrating multi-dimensional situation awareness and three-stage resilience management. An improved Transformer-MAML model is adopted to build a multi-timescale situation awareness engine, with a meta-learning algorithm to realize rapid adaptation under extreme weather shocks, enabling accurate output prediction of massive heterogeneous resources. A hierarchical management mechanism covering normal risk planning, emergency energy dispatching, and blackout recovery is designed, which coordinates electricity, heat and gas components via a fast decomposition algorithm, and realizes independent black start through distributed power and energy storage coordinated control. Real high-altitude scenario simulations verify that this method reduces operating costs, and significantly enhances the survivability and operational resilience of P-CES under extreme power accidents.

detail.title: The Personal Productivity Command Center: Why 2026 Is the Year of Intelligent Orchestration
detail.abstract: Context switching represents one of the most significant yet underaddressed productivity challenges facing modern knowledge workers. Research indicates the average digital worker toggles between applications approximately 1,200 times daily, with each interruption requiring an average of 23 minutes to regain focus (Mark, 2008). This fragmented attention pattern costs the global economy an estimated $450 billion annually in lost productivity (Gallup/Loom Research, 2024). This paper examines the evolution of AI productivity tools from isolated assistants (2023) through integrated copilots (2024) to autonomous agents (2025), and proposes a framework for the next phase: the Personal Productivity Command Center. Unlike existing approaches that require manual context transfer between tools, the command center paradigm establishes an orchestration layer that unifies email, calendar, task management, and communication tools with AI-powered intelligence. The proposed four-layer framework comprises: (1) an Integration Layer connecting core work applications via the Model Context Protocol (MCP); (2) an Intelligence Layer leveraging large language models for categorization, prioritization, and relationship identification; (3) an Orchestration Layer coordinating automated actions across connected systems through AI agents; and (4) an Interface Layer providing unified visibility for human decision-making. Drawing on practitioner experience building and operating unified workspaces using both Claude Cowork (Anthropic's research preview, available via Claude Desktop) and Claude Code (within VS Code), integrated with multiple MCP servers spanning Gmail, Calendar, Slack, Linear, GitHub, and task management, this paper provides a practical methodology for individuals and small teams to implement personal command centers. Two implementation paths are identified: a no-code path via Claude Cowork accessible to non-technical knowledge workers, and an advanced developer path via Claude Code for full customization. Observational data from operating the AI Operations Community, where practitioners learn to build Productivity HQ workspaces, supplements the author's personal implementation experience. The analysis suggests that the transition from fragmented AI tools to unified orchestration represents a fundamental shift in personal productivity methodology. Early adopters who build these systems gain competitive advantages through reduced context switching, clearer prioritization, and more time available for focused work.

detail.title: A Hybrid Typology of Tokenomic Constructions for Tokenization of the Value Creation Chain in the Real Estate Sector: Stochastic Modelling of Resilience
detail.abstract:
This paper presents the results of stochastic modelling of a hybrid tokenomic construction for the residential real estate sector, developed by the author in 2022 (copyright registration certificate No. 23957, Republic of Kazakhstan) and subsequently classified within the framework of the SDA Methodology for tokenization of the value creation chain (2026) as a hybrid of circulation and investment potentials. The present work does not disclose the internal tokenomic architecture, which is protected under copyright; instead, it presents the methodology and results of a computer simulation confirming the economic viability of the construction.

The simulator is implemented as a three-module stochastic system combining a deterministic mathematical core, a vectorized agent-based model of the secondary market, and Monte Carlo testing of macroeconomic factors with a Cholesky-based correlation structure. A total of 3,000 independent simulations were performed (1,000 for each of three scenarios: baseline, stress, and case-switching) on a hypothetical portfolio of 100 objects with a total value of 4.95 billion Kazakhstani tenge, at an interest rate of 18% per annum and a term of 25 years.

Key findings: (1) mathematical consistency of the construction is confirmed by the fulfilment of eight fundamental identities to machine precision; (2) the probability of positive net present value at the portfolio level remains at 100% even in the stress scenario; (3) the realized investor yield declines by only 1.28 percentage points under a severe macroeconomic shock; (4) an embedded automatic stabilizer of the secondary market is identified — trading volume contracts by 58% under stress, preventing cascade effects characteristic of classical securitization. An objective distinction is drawn between mathematically robust properties of the model and estimated parameters that require empirical calibration.

detail.abstract: As Generative AI (GenAI) shifts the human role in software development from creative authorship to review-centric oversight, the foundational assumptions of software traceability are undergoing a systemic failure. This paper defines Ghost Intent-the experiential manifestation of Authorless Traceability Collapse (ATC)-a structural condition where engineering rationale evaporates postgeneration, leaving only behavioral remnants embedded in artifacts. We argue that Ghost Intent invalidates long-standing Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) assumptions and produces a debug cost inversion, where accelerated generation is decoupled from the non-linear expansion of diagnostic effort. Beyond technical debt, this paper positions Ghost Intent as a first-order governance and institutional risk. By articulating its formal characteristics, observability signals, and multi-dimensional risk profile, we establish a critical conceptual vocabulary for AI-native SDLC formalization. This framework provides a basis for future regulatory compliance, decision-behavior governance, and the mitigation of "epistemic opacity" in AI-augmented organizational knowledge.

detail.abstract: This paper addresses the problem of multi-controller collaborative scheduling and energy efficiency optimization in automotive cyber-physical systems (CPS). A flat semi-dormant multi-controller (FSDMC) structure is proposed for a specialized CPS platform, referred to as the arbitrated networked control system incorporating dual-channel communication. The model utilizes a finite-capacity queuing system of type $M^{[X]}/M/c/K$, which supports batch data transmission and incorporates an N-policy along with synchronous multiple working vacations (SMWV) for a subset of servers. The FSDMC is represented as a quasi-birth-and-death process to derive the stationary probability distribution of the system. Using this queuing formulation, multiple performance indices are quantified to construct a nonlinear cost-performance ratio (CPR) function. An optimization framework is then developed to minimize the CPR. To identify the optimal parameter settings under stability restrictions, a particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm is applied. The experimental results validate the effectiveness of the proposed model. Finally, a sensitivity analysis is conducted to examine the influence of key parameters on both system performance and the CPR.

detail.abstract: This paper studies the effectiveness of risk management, one of the two channels identified by the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS, 2024) as those through which the financial system contributes to physical risk adaptation in the European Union (EU). We assess the efficacy of Level 3 prudential regulations in encouraging banks to include physical risk adaptation in their risk management and client engagement strategies. Our analysis adopts a broad perspective, encompassing not only prudential risk management but also, and in our view more importantly, prudential transparency regulation, given the positive leverage that stakeholders can exert to incentivise adaptation efforts. Our findings suggest that banks should consistently integrate physical risk adaptation into their stress tests, transition plans and Pillar III disclosures. Transition plans must address physical hazards, exposure and vulnerability and must set adaptation targets. Adaptation measures should be treated as risk mitigants reflected in losses given default (LGDs), with the severity and consistency of those losses being reflected in transition plans and stress tests.

detail.abstract: Enterprise AI adoption is not a technology decision, it is an operating model transformation. detail.title: Multi-objective Optimization of Train Service Design in Suburban Rail with Composite Strategies
detail.abstract: To address the issue of unbalanced passenger flow in suburban rail systems, a bi-objective optimization model for train service planning is developed, integrating express/local operations, short-turning, and cross-line operational strategies. The model aims to simultaneously minimize operator costs and passenger travel time within a two-route network. A Two-Stage Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II with Hybrid Initialization (HI-TS-NSGA-II) is proposed as the solution approach. In the first stage, a heuristic algorithm is applied to minimize the number of train services under given demand and capacity constraints; in the second stage, an enhanced NSGA-II incorporating an embedded repair mechanism is utilized. Computational experiments based on the Guangzhou suburban rail system show that HI-TS-NSGA-II significantly improves computational efficiency and reduces the number of iterations required for solving the model. Analytical results further reveal that passenger travel time is approximately 1.5 times more sensitive to variations in passenger flow than operator costs. Under the Composite Operation Mode (COM), increasing the Proportion of Express Trains (PET) from 37.0% to 41.6% leads to a 29.3% increase in operator costs while reducing passenger travel time by 17.3%. Although the Proportion of Short-turning Trains (PST) exhibits inverse correlations within individual trend lines, a PST of 9% is identified as the Pareto-optimal solution across multiple scenarios. System-level analysis confirms the superiority of COM, achieving a reduction of over 6.8% in total social cost and over 7.6% in Average Travel Time of Passengers (ATTP) compared to alternative operational modes.

Despite $2.9 trillion in projected business value and organizational investment at scale, no cross-platform, behavior-anchored, governance-integrated instrument exists to measure how well a specific person performs within that partnership at the individual level. This paper addresses that gap by introducing Human-AI Collaborative Intelligence (HACI) as the measurement science discipline that operationalizes augmented intelligence at the individual level. detail.abstract:
Data has become the most strategic resource of the 21st century. However, despite the rapid expansion of the global data economy, most nations lack sovereign institutional frameworks capable of governing how data is accessed, exchanged, and economically utilized.

This paper introduces the concept of the National Data Trust (NDT), a sovereign institutional model designed to govern the national data economy. Functionally analogous to a central bank for data, the NDT establishes governance frameworks, regulatory standards, and trusted infrastructure for secure data exchange while enabling the creation of regulated data markets.

The paper outlines the institutional architecture, technical framework, economic model, and implementation strategy required to establish an NDT at the national level. It further explores the potential for a global network of interoperable National Data Trusts, enabling secure cross-border data exchange while preserving national sovereignty.

The NDT framework offers a structured approach for nations to reclaim digital sovereignty, unlock economic value from data, and participate in the global data economy under transparent and balanced governance conditions.

Enterprise software organizations maintain deep investments in proprietary and third-party component libraries (Angular Material, Material UI, Ant Design, and countless bespoke systems) that encode years of brand decisions, accessibility engineering, and interaction patterns accumulated over product lifetimes. The rapid adoption of AI-driven chat interfaces has introduced a fracture: teams must choose between their established design systems and the generic rendering layer imposed by existing generative UI frameworks. This paper introduces AbstractUI, not as a competing wire protocol, but as the missing enterprise automation bridge that sits upstream of today's rendering standards.

AbstractUI defines the Docket, a machine-readable JSON document describing component definitions, design token hierarchies, layout composition patterns, and framework-specific adapter mappings. The Docket is auto generated from existing codebases via a TypeScript Compiler API scanner, requiring zero manual annotation for Angular Material, MUI, Ant Design, Chakra UI, and other major libraries. detail.abstract: Employment-based immigration compliance in the United States has historically been assessed through discrete checkpoints: petition filings, adjudication outcomes, and periodic audits. Between these checkpoints, sponsorship behavior evolves in ways that existing oversight frameworks do not capture. This paper introduces a framework for continuous integrity measurement of H-1B sponsorship behavior using publicly available federal datasets from the Department of Labor and U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services. The framework defines integrity as the alignment between what employers claim in their filings and what observable data patterns reveal about their actual behavior. We organize measurement into five behavioral dimensions-Wage Integrity, Filing Integrity, Role Integrity, Outcome Integrity, and Program Integrityand specify six metrics for an initial implementation. Applied to 2.37 million H-1B Labor Condition Application filings across fiscal years 2022 through 2025, the framework yields four findings that illustrate its analytical utility, including evidence consistent with a counterintuitive market composition shift in wage-level filing patterns and a novel metric for templated filing behavior. The framework is designed to complement, not replace, existing legal and regulatory oversight, and to provide a foundation for continuous sponsorship integrity intelligence in both human and AI-assisted decision contexts.

detail.abstract: Although financial market fluctuations that move together are often interpreted as evidence of a global financial cycle, driven by macroeconomic and financial shocks, they may also result from spillover effects generated by local financial linkages and interdependencies among countries. This study is among the first to jointly test the impact of global common factors and local spatial spillover effects by integrating both mechanisms into a unified dynamic spatial panel data model. The global common factors are determined not only by means of a latent dynamic factor derived from a large panel of monthly data on financial variables, but also by means of cross-sectional averages of the dependent variable. Local spatial spillover effects are determined by means of spatial lags determined by neighboring countries through different metrics of proximity. Using quarterly data on national financial cycles in credit and equity markets in 25 countries over the period 1997-2019, along with four distance matrices and two control variables, we find that the dependence between countries in national financial cycles stems from a combination of all the proposed model elements. In addition, geographic distance appears to be the best performing representation of the local spillover effects between national credit cycles and economic distance between national equity cycles.

detail.title: A Variance-Aware Benchmarking Workflow for Reproducible Deep Learning in Cervical Cytology: A Pilot Study on SIPaKMeD
detail.abstract: Background and objective: Deep learning-based cervical cytology classification has been widely studied, yet benchmarking on small public datasets remains heterogeneous and often underreports run-to-run variability. On constrained medical imaging benchmarks, small apparent performance gains may reflect evaluation design as much as genuine model advantage. This creates a practical problem for early-stage model selection: point estimates alone may overstate ranking certainty when uncertainty reporting and development-confirmation separation are limited.Methods: To address this issue, we implemented a variance-aware, test-isolated benchmarking workflow for reproducible early-stage evaluation in cervical cytology. As a pilot study, we applied this workflow to a ResNet-50 baseline and two lightweight dual-pooling channel-attention variants on the SIPaKMeD dataset. The workflow used a fixed image-level 70/15/15 train/validation/test split, merged the training and validation subsets into a development set, performed 5-fold stratified cross-validation only within that development set, and repeated evaluation across three random seeds per configuration, yielding 54 total training runs across all models. Performance was summarized using mean accuracy, dispersion metrics, empirical run-level descriptive intervals, and exploratory paired sensitivity analyses.Results: Across repeated development runs, mean cross-validation accuracy ranged from 98.04% to 98.19%, with substantial overlap in empirical descriptive intervals. Within this workflow, ranking by mean performance diverged from ranking by variability, and the development-stage ordering did not remain stable at the held-out internal confirmation stage. These findings indicate that, on constrained public benchmarks, marginal apparent gains may be highly sensitive to the benchmarking workflow and should be interpreted cautiously.Conclusions: The main contribution of this study is methodological rather than architectural. Using a concrete cervical cytology benchmark, the proposed workflow makes ranking instability more visible through repeated evaluation, explicit uncertainty characterization, and development-confirmation separation. It may therefore serve as a practical early-stage benchmarking template for vetting candidate models before patient-level, slide-level, or prospective clinical validation.

detail.abstract: We study how AI affects compensation and job design when performance depends on workers' non-contractible effort. In a principal–agent model with limited liability, AI reduces effort costs but disproportionately lowers the cost of achieving satisfactory performance. This raises the incentive cost of sustaining high effort and can induce firms to replace high-wage, high-effort good jobs with low-wage, low-effort bad jobs, even when good jobs create more total surplus. As a result, AI can lower wages, reduce worker welfare, and even depress profits. If workers can adopt AI unilaterally, adoption occurs even when the resulting equilibrium harms both parties; when adoption requires worker cooperation, resistance is strongest where AI erodes rents embodied in good jobs. In a search-and-matching extension, endogenous outside options amplify these forces, reinforcing a bad-job economy and potentially reducing employment.

title: The Urban-Rural Gap in Local Market Access: Evidence from Grocery Demand
affiliations: , University of Bern and University of Duisburg-Essen

detail.title: The Urban-Rural Gap in Local Market Access: Evidence from Grocery Demand

publicationDetails.journalName: CESifo Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper leverages quasi-experimental variation from store openings and 1.5 billion grocery transactions to causally estimate the distance elasticity of grocery expenditures (−1.47) and the spatial extent of local consumption areas (approximately 16 minutes of car travel time). We embed these estimates in a nested CES demand framework to construct a granular index of local market access for nearly 350,000 grid cells (100×100m) across Switzerland. Urban areas enjoy nearly twice the consumption access of rural areas, with the 90th-to-10th percentile ratio nationally exceeding four. Compensating variation calculations show that low-income and elderly households would benefit disproportionately from improved local market access. Finally, we document that market access varies predominantly between locations, whereas income differs mostly within locations—the two dimensions are nearly orthogonal. This suggests that place-based retail policies and income-based transfers address fundamentally different dimensions of spatial inequality and should be regarded as complements.
